necessary_context.content: Problem (1) uses f:R^m x R^n -> R on full Euclidean spaces. A saddle satisfies f(x*,y)<=f(x*,y*)<=f(x,y*) for every x,y. Norms are Euclidean.
necessary_context.locator: Main PDF pp.1,3, Problem (1), notation and Definition 3
necessary_context.name: Unconstrained saddle problem and Euclidean norm

necessary_context.applies_to: Theorem 7 and its selected EG tuning
necessary_context.content: f is continuously differentiable; for every fixed y, f(.,y) is mu_x-strongly convex, and for every fixed x, f(x,.) is mu_y-strongly concave, with positive constants. Definition 2 uses the quadratic term mu/2 times squared Euclidean distance. Set mu=min(mu_x,mu_y); denote the unique saddle by (x*,y*).
necessary_context.locator: Main PDF p.3, Definition 2 and Assumption 2
necessary_context.name: Strong convexity and strong concavity

necessary_context.applies_to: Selected EG contraction; do not replace the joint operator bound by L
necessary_context.content: The prose of Assumption 3 states that gradient_x is L_x-Lipschitz in x and L_xy-Lipschitz in y, while gradient_y is L_y-Lipschitz in y and L_yx-Lipschitz in x, uniformly in the other block. L=max{L_x,L_xy,L_y,L_yx}, kappa=L/mu, and r_k=||x_k-x*||^2+||y_k-y*||^2. The operator F=(gradient_x f,-gradient_y f) has a 2L Lipschitz bound, as explicitly used in supplement Section 8.9.
necessary_context.locator: Main PDF p.4, Assumption 3, Remark 1, Eq.(2); supplement p.12, Section 8.9
necessary_context.name: Block Lipschitz constants and distance
